sentences.en: On Tuesday, Democratic Socialist Francesca Hong lost the Democratic nomination for governor in Wisconsin in an upset after leading by double digits in the polls.

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Chief Political Analyst Nate Cohn, helps make sense of those conflicting outcomes and explains what they tell us about the state of the populist left

sentences.en: in Democratic politics.

sentences.en: Nate, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 内特，欢迎回到《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: It's wonderful to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.

sentences.en: Great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: So we want to talk today about what this moment means for the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天想聊聊这个时刻对民主党意味着什么。

sentences.en: For the past 10 years, it feels as though we've been talking about this divide in the party between the progressive left and the moderate establishment.
sentences.zh: 在过去10年里，感觉我们一直在讨论党内进步左翼与温和建制派之间的分歧。

sentences.en: And it feels like the story of this primary season for Democrats is to what extent is that progressive flank ascendant in the party and in national politics?
sentences.zh: 而对于民主党人来说，这次初选季的故事似乎在于：进步派在党内和国家政治中的崛起程度究竟有多大？

sentences.en: In the last two weeks, one of those candidates narrowly won in Michigan and another narrowly lost in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 在过去两周里，其中一位候选人在密歇根州险胜，另一位在威斯康星州险败。

sentences.en: I don't totally know what to make of that.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道该怎么看待这件事。

sentences.en: It feels a little confusing to me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有点困惑。

sentences.en: But fortunately, that's what we have you for.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，这就是我们请你来的原因。

sentences.en: So, Nate, what should we make of that?
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，我们该如何看待这件事？

sentences.en: Well, fortunately, I think it isn't very confusing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，幸运的是，我觉得这并不怎么令人困惑。

sentences.en: It's pretty clarifying.
sentences.zh: 这相当具有启发意义。

sentences.en: We've had two races in two weeks in states that are presidential battleground states, reasonably representative of the country politically in different ways,
sentences.zh: 我们在两周内在两个州进行了两场竞选，这两个州都是总统大选的摇摆州，在政治上以不同方式合理地代表了整个国家，

sentences.en: where the progressive left has essentially been tied a little bit ahead or a little bit behind with their establishment rivals.
sentences.zh: 在这些选举中，进步左翼基本上与他们的建制派对手打成平手，略微领先或略微落后。

sentences.en: This is pretty different from what we've seen over most of the last 10 years, when the progressive left has basically only been reliably competitive
sentences.zh: 这与我们过去10年大部分时间看到的情况截然不同，当时进步左翼基本上只在民主党优势明显、年轻、受教育程度极高的城市地区

sentences.en: in heavily Democratic, young, highly educated urban areas.
sentences.zh: 才具有稳定的竞争力。

sentences.en: Now, that can happen twice in two weeks, after all, in presidential battleground states, and therefore, perhaps even nationwide.
sentences.zh: 现在，这种事在两周内发生了两次，毕竟是在总统大选摇摆州，因此，甚至可能在全国范围内也是如此。

sentences.en: That still comes with limits.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然有其局限性。

sentences.en: There are large parts of these states where the progressive candidates aren't faring very well, and that suggests there are also large parts of the country
sentences.zh: 在这些州的许多地方，进步派候选人的表现并不好，这表明全国也有很大一部分地区

sentences.en: where the progressive left wouldn't fare very well.
sentences.zh: 是进步左翼无法取得好成绩的。

sentences.en: But this represents a really significant improvement in their standing within the Democratic Party compared to where they seem to stand just a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 但与几年前他们在党内的地位相比，这代表了他们在民主党内地位的显著提升。

sentences.en: — Okay, I want to dig deeper into what you actually mean by the limits that these candidates are facing and what they've actually gained.
sentences.zh: ——好的，我想深入探讨一下你所说的这些候选人面临的局限性以及他们实际获得了什么，到底是什么意思。

sentences.en: But before we do, can you just spell out what we mean exactly when we talk about the left here?
sentences.zh: 但在我们开始之前，你能具体解释一下我们这里所说的“左翼”到底是指什么吗？

sentences.en: Like, who are these candidates?
sentences.zh: 比如，这些候选人都是谁？

sentences.en: I heard a sigh.
sentences.zh: 我听到了一声叹息。

sentences.en: — It's a little challenging to define.
sentences.zh: ——这有点难以定义。

sentences.en: We don't just mean progressives, after all, right?
sentences.zh: 毕竟我们不只是指进步派，对吧？

sentences.en: Progressives have been winning Democratic primaries for decades.
sentences.zh: 进步派赢得民主党初选已经有几十年的历史了。

sentences.en: Half of Democrats in Congress could be said to be progressives in some form or another.
sentences.zh: 国会中有一半的民主党人可以说在某种程度上都是进步派。

sentences.en: We mean a new kind of young, activist-backed candidate of, for lack of a better word, the progressive left.
sentences.zh: 我们指的是一种由年轻、激进主义者支持的新型候选人，用一个不太恰当的词来说，就是进步左翼。

sentences.en: I think the core of this new activist progressive left are the self-identified Democratic socialists,
sentences.zh: 我认为这个新的激进进步左翼的核心是自称的民主社会主义者，

sentences.en: Mamdani, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and their allies.
sentences.zh: 马姆达尼、亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科特斯以及他们的盟友。

sentences.en: Beyond them, though, there is a group of politicians who looks a lot like them, but does not necessarily characterize themselves as Democratic socialists.
sentences.zh: 不过，在他们之外，还有一群政客，看起来和他们很像，但不一定自称为民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: — Like who?
sentences.zh: ——比如谁？

sentences.en: — Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan is one great example.
sentences.zh: ——密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德博士就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: He was endorsed by both Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez, but he doesn't call himself a Democratic socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 他得到了桑德斯和奥卡西奥-科特斯的共同背书，但他不自称为民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: But it's hard to see why he's not a Democratic socialiSt.
sentences.zh: 但很难看出他为什么不是民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: He doesn't distinguish himself from them on the issues in many ways, and he's comfortable allying with them,
sentences.zh: 他在许多问题上没有把自己和他们区分开来，而且他乐于与他们结盟，

sentences.en: and importantly, allying with them against the mainstream of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，他乐于与他们结盟来对抗民主党的主流派。

sentences.en: — So data-wise, when you look at the numbers, which are your bread and butter, you're looking at candidates who are either members of the Democratic Socialists organization
sentences.zh: ——所以从数据来看，当你审视数字——这是你的看家本领——你看到的是那些既是民主社会主义组织成员的候选人，

sentences.en: or are effectively part of that platform.
sentences.zh: 或者是该政治纲领的实际参与者。

sentences.en: They are aligned with many aspects of it.
sentences.zh: 他们与该纲领的许多方面保持一致。

sentences.en: — Yeah, there are a lot of different ways to define it, but they stand apart from not only the establishment moderate in the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: ——是的，定义它的方法有很多种，但他们不仅与民主党内的温和建制派划清界限，

sentences.en: but also the kind of progressive candidate who's been winning in the Democratic Party for a long time.
sentences.zh: 也与长期以来在民主党内获胜的那种进步派候选人不同。

sentences.en: — Okay, and the question going into the last couple of weeks, right, was whether this progressive left could win, not just in places like New York, deep blue areas,
sentences.zh: ——好的，在过去两周之前的那个问题是，这种进步左翼是否能够获胜，不仅在像纽约这样深蓝的地区，

sentences.en: but in purple areas, states like Michigan and Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 还能在紫色地区，比如密歇根州和威斯康星州获胜。

sentences.en: So let's get into what we learned from the two Democratic primaries in those states.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们来探讨一下我们从这两个州的民主党初选中学到了什么。

sentences.en: — I think the most obvious thing we learned is that, yes, the progressive left can compete in these states.
sentences.zh: ——我认为我们学到的最明显的事情是，是的，进步左翼可以在这些州参与竞争。

sentences.en: Now, it's worth noting that each of these races are idiosyncratic primaries.
sentences.zh: 现在，值得一提的是，这些初选中的每一场都具有其独特的个性。

sentences.en: They have different candidates with different strengths and weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有不同的候选人，有着各自的优势和劣势。

sentences.en: In Michigan, in a primary for U.S.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州，在一场美国参议院初选中，

sentences.en: Senate,
sentences.zh: 民主党人阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德博士开展了一场赢得了全国各地进步派极大热情的竞选活动，他的竞争对手是国会女议员海莉·史蒂文斯，

sentences.en: Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed ran a campaign that received a lot of enthusiasm from progressives across the country, and he ran against Congresswoman Haley Stevens,
sentences.zh: 她是一位有建制派支持的候选人，拥有数千万美元广告资金的优势，尽管她也有自己的负面资产，

sentences.en: an establishment-backed candidate who had the advantage of tens of millions of dollars in advertisements, even though she had her own liabilities,
sentences.zh: 比如在一个以色列相当不得人心的时候，她却是一个非常坚定的以色列支持者。

sentences.en: like being a really strong supporter of Israel at a time when that's pretty unpopular.
sentences.zh: 而在普通民主党人中。

sentences.en: among rank-and-file Democrats.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州的情况完全不同。

sentences.en: There was a totally different set of circumstances in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 那是一场州长竞选，民主社会主义者弗朗西斯卡·洪并没有发起一场特别强劲的竞选。

sentences.en: That was a race for governor, where Francesca Hong, a Democratic socialist, did not run an especially strong race.
sentences.zh: 她没有获得像亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科特斯或伯尼·桑德斯这样的人的背书。

sentences.en: She did not earn endorsements from people like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez or Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 她有在社交媒体上发帖和发表言论的黑历史，这让她看起来并不像一个非常引人注目的政治人物。

sentences.en: She had a long track record of posting and making remarks on social media that did not make her seem like a terribly compelling politician.
sentences.zh: 竞选的最后一周，大部分时间都用来争论她在社交媒体上关于自己对感恩节和万圣节有意见的言论。

sentences.en: Much of the final week of the campaign was spent litigating social media posts about how she had problems with Thanksgiving and Halloween.
sentences.zh: 这不一定是进步左翼推出的最好候选人。

sentences.en: This was not necessarily the best candidate that the progressive left has put forward.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，民主党温和派在这场竞选中几乎没能推出一位候选人。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the moderate wing of the Democratic Party almost failed to put forward a candidate in this race.
sentences.zh: 它经历了多位潜在的领跑者，他们加入竞选又退出竞选，在某些情况下甚至重新加入竞选。

sentences.en: It cycled through multiple potential frontrunners who entered the race and dropped out of the race and in some cases came back into the race.
sentences.zh: 直到竞选的最后几天，该党才似乎团结在大卫·克劳利身后，他是一位来自密尔沃基县的相对不知名的候选人，

sentences.en: And only in the final days of the campaign did the party appear to coalesce behind David Crowley, who was a relatively unknown candidate from Milwaukee County,
sentences.zh: 但在竞选期间，他并没有什么全州范围的声誉，也没有数千万美元的资金支持。

sentences.en: but who did not have any statewide reputation or tens of millions of dollars backing him during the campaign.
sentences.zh: 但尽管我们刚刚分析的这两场不同竞选之间存在种种差异，我们最终还是得到了基本相同的结局。

sentences.en: But despite all the differences that we just worked through between these two different races, we still ended up with the same basic result.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州和威斯康星州最终几乎不相上下。

sentences.en: Michigan and Wisconsin ended up essentially dead even.
sentences.zh: 进步派候选人险胜了一场，又险败了另一场。

sentences.en: The progressive candidate narrowly won one race and narrowly lost the other.
sentences.zh: 但故事基本是一样的。

sentences.en: But the story was basically the same.
sentences.zh: 相同的族群在每一次竞选背后保持一致。

sentences.en: The same demographic groups aligned between each ones.
sentences.zh: 他们表现出相同的优势。

sentences.en: They showed the same strengths.
sentences.zh: 他们表现出相同的劣势。

sentences.en: They showed the same weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 结果如此相似这一事实表明，塑造这些竞选中正在发生的事情的最强大因素

sentences.en: And the fact that the results are so similar suggests that the most powerful factor that's shaping what's happening in these races
sentences.zh: 是全国民主党内部这些潜在的大分歧，而不是这些竞选各自的独特性。

sentences.en: are these underlying big divides in the National Democratic Party, not the idiosyncrasies of these races.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为我们可以从中汲取很多教训。

sentences.en: And so I think we can learn a lot from them as a result.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 内特，请为我们剖析这些潜在的分歧。

sentences.en: Nate, walk us through those underlying divides.
sentences.zh: 支持这些进步左翼候选人的都是哪些族群？

sentences.en: What were the demographic groups that aligned behind these progressive left candidates?
sentences.zh: 我认为你必须从年龄开始说起。

sentences.en: I think you have to start with age.
sentences.zh: 推动进步左翼支持的最明显的事情，无论是当你逐个选区、逐个县去查看实际结果时，还是在民调中，

sentences.en: The most obvious thing that's driving support for the progressive left, both in the actual results when you look at it precinct by precinct or county by county, and in the polling,
sentences.zh: 就是年轻选民压倒性地支持进步左翼候选人，而年长选民则支持温和建制派候选人。

sentences.en: is that young voters overwhelmingly back the candidates of the progressive left, while older voters support moderate establishment candidates.
sentences.zh: 民调显示，他们赢得了压倒性的优势，比如占投票率的60%、70%，甚至80%。

sentences.en: The polls say that they won overwhelming margins, like 60, 70, maybe even 80% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在这些州最年轻的街区和选区中所看到的，特别是在几所大型旗舰大学的大学校园里，

sentences.en: And that's what we see in the youngest neighborhoods and precincts of these states, particularly on the college campuses of the big flagship universities,
sentences.zh: 比如密歇根大学或威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校。

sentences.en: like the University of Michigan or the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
sentences.zh: 在安娜堡的某些选区，埃尔-赛义德赢得了95%的选票。

sentences.en: There are precincts where El-Sayed won 95% of the vote in Ann Arbor.
sentences.zh: 还有一些选区，用一个不太恰当的词来形容，就是密尔沃基年轻、时髦、正在士绅化的街区，你在那里也会看到类似的情况，也许不是95%的悬殊差距，

sentences.en: There are precincts that are sort of, for lack of a better word, young, hip, gentrifying neighborhoods in Milwaukee, where you see similarly, maybe not 95% lopsided margins,
sentences.zh: 但即使对弗朗西斯卡·洪来说，也有70%、80%的差距。

sentences.en: but 70, 80% margins, even for Francesca Hong.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: That is crazy.
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: Why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 我们是否大致了解是什么促使年轻选民而不是年长选民倾向于这些候选人？

sentences.en: Do we have a sense of what is driving young voters and not older voters to these candidates?
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是我们在民主党内已经看到几十年的故事。

sentences.en: Well, in some sense, this is a story that we've seen in the Democratic Party for decades now.
sentences.zh: 步入成年、对国家感到不满并希望看到改变的年轻选民，

sentences.en: Young voters who come of age and are dissatisfied with the country and want to see changes,
sentences.zh: 自然会寻找比民主党过去所提供的还要更偏左的东西。

sentences.en: then look naturally to something that's even farther to the left of what the Democratic Party has offered in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 然后这就是年轻选民参与竞选的理念，无论是20世纪60年代的民权运动，还是巴拉克·奥巴马对阵希拉里·克林顿，

sentences.en: And then that's what the young voters campaign on, whether it's in the 1960s and the civil rights movement, Barack Obama versus Hillary Clinton,
sentences.zh: 又或者是现在的民主社会主义者对阵奥巴马时代的传统主流进步主义。

sentences.en: or now the Democratic Socialists against the kind of mainstream progressivism of the Obama era.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种情绪被一些特定因素进一步放大了，比如年轻人认为他们在当今后金融危机时代的经济中所面临的挣扎。

sentences.en: I think that sentiment's been supercharged by some particular factors to this moment, the struggles that young people think they have in today's post-financial crisis economy.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为同样值得一提的是，用一个不太恰当的词来说，当今时代的思想气候是如何塑造年轻选民观点的。

sentences.en: And I think it's also worth mentioning the way that, for lack of a better word, the intellectual climate of today's age shapes the views of young voters.

sentences.en: There are ideas from academia about capitalism and sexism and white supremacy and intersectionality

sentences.en: that are all very familiar to us today, but which an older generation of college graduates had never heard of, even while we're all familiar with Judith Butler or something.

sentences.en: So I think this really shapes the kind of ideas that young, college-educated voters are receptive to.

sentences.en: it's now being channeled into a particular set of ideas that older generations don't even know about, let alone support.

sentences.en: What else does the data say about the divides here, about the coalitions?
sentences.zh: 我认为第二大分歧，也许通过反过来问“温和派在哪里表现最好”会更容易讨论。

sentences.en: I think the next biggest divide, it's maybe easier to talk about by flipping it around and saying, where did the moderates do best?
sentences.zh: 在这两个州，高收入街区、高收入选民都是温和派的主要优势区域，

sentences.en: And in both states, high-income neighborhoods, high-income voters stand out as a major area of strength for moderates,
sentences.zh: 收入总体上就是这里的关键分水岭之一。

sentences.en: with income in general just being one of the key fault lines here.
sentences.zh: 在人们收入达到15万或更多美元的街区，温和派候选人以二比一获胜的情况经常发生。

sentences.en: In neighborhoods where people make $150,000 or more, there were often cases where the moderate candidates won by two to one.
sentences.zh: 如果进步左翼总体上、这些候选人具体而言在政策上确实代表了什么的话，我认为这不应该太令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I don't think this should be terribly surprising if the progressive left in general, and these candidates specifically really stand for anything in terms of policy.
sentences.zh: 那就是向国家的大亨、企业和财富不平等发起挑战。

sentences.en: It's to take on the billionaires, corporations, and wealth inequality in the country.
sentences.zh: 高收入选民对这种候选人格外犹豫，这在情理之中。

sentences.en: And it makes sense that high-income voters would be particularly hesitant to embrace those kind of candidates.
sentences.zh: 当你低于高收入群体时，结果中就会出现更多的异质性。

sentences.en: When you go below the high-income group, there's a lot more heterogeneity in the results.
sentences.zh: 其中一部分归结为年龄，对吧？

sentences.en: And part of that comes down to age, right?
sentences.zh: 有些低收入选民是年轻的大学生或刚毕业的人，他们非常支持进步派。

sentences.en: There are low-income voters who are young college kids or people just out of college who are very supportive of the progressives.
sentences.zh: 然后还有低收入的老年选民，而这些低收入的老年选民可能仍然支持建制派。

sentences.en: And then there are also low-income older voters, and those low-income older voters may still support the establishment.
sentences.zh: 我想还有一个需要指出的点，那就是关于种族的的分歧。

sentences.en: And I think there's one additional point to make, and that's the divide over race.
sentences.zh: 在这两场竞选中，建制派候选人在黑人选民中表现得非常好。

sentences.en: The establishment candidates in both of these contests did really well among black voters.
sentences.zh: 现在，值得注意的是，正如我所提到的，这两场竞选都具有独特性，

sentences.en: Now, it's worth noting that, as I've mentioned, both these races are idiosyncratic,
sentences.zh: 而且两位亲建制派的候选人都有特别能吸引黑人选民的理由。

sentences.en: and both of the establishment-friendly candidates had particularly strong cases for black voters.
sentences.zh: 海莉·史蒂文斯大肆宣扬她与奥巴马政府在底特律汽车业救助计划上的合作。

sentences.en: Haley Stevens trumpeted her work with the Obama administration on the Detroit auto bailout.
sentences.zh: 大卫·克劳利本人就是非裔美国人，因此他对密尔沃基的黑人选民有着天然的吸引力。

sentences.en: David Crowley is African-American himself, so he had natural appeal to Milwaukee's black voters.
sentences.zh: 但值得注意的是，我们一次又一次地看到，在黑人选民中，受建制派支持的候选人表现得比进步派候选人更好。

sentences.en: But it's worth noting that we have seen over and over again that establishment-backed candidates do better than progressive candidates among black voters.
sentences.zh: 内特，我觉得我在这里变成了一张复读机，但为什么呢？

sentences.en: I feel like I'm turning into a broken record here, Nate, but why?
sentences.zh: 我们知道这是为什么吗？

sentences.zh: 我们知道这是为什么吗？

sentences.en: I think the easiest place to start is to remember that black voters almost unanimously support Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我觉得最容易入手的切入点，是记住黑人选民几乎是一致支持民主党的。

sentences.en: And many black voters support Democrats regardless of their views on the issues.
sentences.zh: 而且许多黑人选民无论对具体议题持何种看法，都会支持民主党。

sentences.en: So there are many more moderate or even conservative black voters who vote for Democrats than other racial groups,
sentences.zh: 因此，相比其他族裔，有更多温和派甚至保守派黑人选民投票给民主党，

sentences.en: because for other racial groups, the moderate and conservative voters would just vote Republican.
sentences.zh: 因为对其他族裔来说，温和派和保守派选民会直接投给共和党。

sentences.en: So in the black primary electorate, you have many more moderate and conservative black voters who, at the very least,
sentences.zh: 所以在黑人初选选民中，你有更多温和派和保守派黑人选民，他们至少

sentences.en: are not exactly receptive to the case for democratic socialism or may even outright oppose it.
sentences.zh: 对民主社会主义的主张并不是那么买账，甚至可能公开反对。

sentences.en: The other thing to keep in mind is that in many democratic primaries as of late, older black voters have turned out at much higher levels than young voters.
sentences.zh: 另一件需要记住的事情是，在最近的许多民主党初选中，年长黑人选民的投票率远高于年轻选民。

sentences.en: It may be the case that young black voters support the progressive candidates in these races,
sentences.zh: 也许年轻黑人选民确实支持这些竞选中的进步派候选人，

sentences.en: and it's just really hard to tell because the turnout among young black voters has been really low.
sentences.zh: 但这真的很难判断，因为年轻黑人选民的投票率实在太低了。

sentences.en: Really, in some ways, it's been really low since the Obama era.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在某种程度上，自奥巴马时代以来投票率就一直很低。

sentences.en: So we have a disproportionately older group of black voters who's participating in these primaries as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我们也有一群比例过高的年长黑人选民参与了这些初选。

sentences.en: And again, old voters, regardless of race, are backing the establishment candidate.
sentences.zh: 而且话说回来，无论什么族裔，老年选民都在支持建制派候选人。

sentences.en: Bottom line, Nate, at this moment, when we see these areas of strength and of weakness for the progressive left being highlighted,
sentences.zh: 内特，说到底，此时此刻，当我们看到进步左翼的这些优势和劣势区域被凸显出来时，

sentences.en: should we think of this movement that Bernie Sanders more or less started in 2016 as ascendant and gaining ground or stalling out?
sentences.zh: 我们应该把伯尼·桑德斯在2016年前后大体上发起的这场运动看作是正在上升、不断取得阵地，还是在停滞不前？

sentences.en: I think we should think of it as ascendant and gaining ground, especially if we bracket Bernie Sanders aside for a second.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们应该把它看作是正在上升并不断取得阵地，特别是如果我们先把伯尼·桑德斯搁置在一边的话。

sentences.en: If you bracket aside his campaign, we've watched the progressive left grow from only occasionally winning a handful of primaries
sentences.zh: 如果你把他的竞选放一边，我们会发现进步左翼已经从偶尔在全国受教育程度最高、

sentences.en: in the nation's most highly educated and democratic cities to now competing statewide in classic battleground states like Michigan and Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 最民主的城市赢得少数几场初选，发展到现在能够在密歇根和威斯康星这样的经典摇摆州进行全州范围的竞争。

sentences.en: That said, this is a very different kind of progressive coalition than the one that Bernie Sanders put together back in 2016.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这是一种非常不同的进步派联盟，与伯尼·桑德斯在2016年拼凑起来的那个联盟截然不同。

sentences.en: And it's different in ways that say a lot about where the progressive movement might be heading in 2028 and beyond.
sentences.zh: 而且它的不同之处在很大程度上说明了进步运动在2028年及以后可能的发展方向。

sentences.en: Nate, describe exactly how the progressive coalition has changed since 2016.
sentences.zh: 内特，请具体描述一下自2016年以来进步派联盟是如何变化的。

sentences.en: The thing to understand, it's worth stepping back and remembering what the Bernie Sanders coalition looked like in 2016 against Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 需要理解的是，我们值得退后一步，回想一下2016年伯尼·桑德斯对抗希拉里·克林顿时的联盟是什么样的。

sentences.en: At its core, there was the same young, progressive, democratic socialist activist group that's still at the core of the progressive movement today.
sentences.zh: 在其核心，有那群年轻的、进步的、民主社会主义积极分子，他们至今仍是进步运动的核心。

sentences.en: But what's changed is the group of voters beyond that democratic socialist core, the sort of swing voters of democratic primary politics,
sentences.zh: 但改变的是民主社会主义核心之外的那群选民，也就是民主党初选政治中的那种摇摆选民，

sentences.en: the people who aren't necessarily true believers, but who preferred Bernie Sanders to his opponent, Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 那些未必是坚定信仰者，但比起对手希拉里·克林顿，更偏爱伯尼·桑德斯的人。

sentences.en: In that election, in 2016, the voters who preferred Sanders to Clinton, even though they weren't true believers,
sentences.zh: 在那场选举中，在2016年，那些比起克林顿更倾向于桑德斯的选民，尽管他们不是坚定信仰者，

sentences.en: were mostly working class and particularly working class white voters.
sentences.zh: 但大多是工人阶级，尤其是白人工人阶级选民。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders swept rural parts of Michigan and Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯横扫了密歇根州和威斯康星州的农村地区。

sentences.en: And he did so in part because he was relentlessly focused on a populist message and in part because Hillary Clinton was sort of the perfect foil on economic populist issues.
sentences.zh: 他做到这一点，部分是因为他坚定不移地专注于民粹主义信息，部分是因为希拉里·克林顿在经济民粹主义议题上简直是完美的衬托。

sentences.en: She had backed NAFTA.
sentences.zh: 她曾支持北美自由贸易协定。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And she, you know, had taken all of this money from speeches, from corporations and so on.
sentences.zh: 而且她，你知道的，从演讲、企业等方面拿了所有的这些钱。

sentences.en: And she also campaigned pretty heavily on identity politics, for lack of a better word, in that election.
sentences.zh: 在那场选举中，她还相当大程度上围绕身份政治进行竞选，如果换个更好的词的话。

sentences.en: She was the candidate trying to rally the supporters of Black Lives Matter.
sentences.zh: 她是那个试图集结“黑人的命也是命”支持者的候选人。

sentences.en: And she was also running as potentially the first female president.
sentences.zh: 而且她当时也是作为潜在的第一位女总统在竞选。

sentences.en: And those were major points of emphasis in her campaign.
sentences.zh: 这些都是她竞选中的重点强调内容。

sentences.en: And together, that seemed to give Bernie Sanders the edge among white working class Democrats across much of the northern United States in particular.
sentences.zh: 两者结合起来，似乎让伯尼·桑德斯在特别是美国北部大部分地区的白人工人阶级民主党人中占据了优势。

sentences.en: And even once she became the nominee, Hillary Clinton still struggled among these voters.
sentences.zh: 而且即使她成为了提名人，希拉里·克林顿在这些选民中仍然举步维艰。

sentences.en: Many of them actually ended up backing Donald Trump and have been part of the Republican coalition really ever since.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人最终实际上支持了唐纳德·特朗普，并且几乎从那时起就一直是共和党联盟的一部分。

sentences.en: And they haven't even been available to candidates of the progressive left in many cases.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，他们甚至不再对进步左翼的候选人开放。

sentences.en: If you were to look at the map of Wisconsin and Michigan the last couple of weeks compared to the 2016 one, they look completely different.
sentences.zh: 如果你把过去几周威斯康星州和密歇根州的地图与2016年的地图进行比较，它们看起来完全不同。

sentences.en: They're not winning those rural areas anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们不再赢得那些农村地区了。

sentences.en: And just say why, Nate, because the core of the argument for a lot of these left-wing candidates is economic populism, right?
sentences.zh: 内特，请说一下原因，因为许多这些左翼候选人的核心论点是经济民粹主义，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, El-Sayed's campaign slogan was money out of politics, money in your pocket, Medicare for all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，埃尔萨耶德的竞选口号是把金钱挤出政治、把钱装进你的口袋、全民医保。

sentences.en: It's absolutely an important part of their message.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是他们信息中重要的一部分。

sentences.en: And as I alluded to earlier, they do tend to do better among lower-income voters than certainly rich voters.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前暗示的那样，与富裕选民相比，他们在低收入选民中的表现确实往往更好。

sentences.en: But this is not necessarily nearly as central to their message as it was to Bernie Sanders' message.
sentences.zh: 但这不一定像对伯尼·桑德斯的信息那样，是他们信息的核心。

sentences.en: And conversely, I'm not sure that today's moderate Democrats are as vulnerable on these issues as Hillary Clinton was.
sentences.zh: 相反，我不确定今天的温和派民主党人在这些议题上是否像希拉里·克林顿那样脆弱。

sentences.en: There is, on balance, compared to 2016, much more emphasis by progressives on non-economic issues, period.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，与2016年相比，进步派对非经济议题的强调要多得多，句号。

sentences.zh: 例如加沙。

sentences.en: as Bernie would put it, the millionaires and the billionaires, right?

sentences.zh: 所以，如果关于你竞选的大部分对话都是关于那些让激进进步派兴奋不已的议题，

sentences.en: the fact that you then try and turn your message back to putting money in people's pockets won't be as powerful as it would be if that were all you were talking about.
sentences.zh: 那么你随后试图将你的信息转回到把钱放进人们口袋的事实，就不会像如果那是你唯一谈论的内容时那样具有冲击力。

sentences.en: And I think it's fair to say that's what the Bernie Sanders campaign did in 2016 that we just don't see from progressives since then.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，这就是伯尼·桑德斯在2016年所做的事情，而我们自那以后在进步派身上就再也没有看到了。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 现在，

sentences.en: today's progressives have made up for this by doing much better than Bernie Sanders did among a different group of voters who were sort of outside that core Democratic Socialist activist base.
sentences.zh: 今天的进步派通过在另一群游离于核心民主社会主义激进派之外的选民中表现得比伯尼·桑德斯好得多，弥补了这一点。

sentences.en: Which is?
sentences.zh: 哪群人？

sentences.en: They're doing much better among, for lack of a better word, kind of mainstream progressive liberals.
sentences.zh: 换个更好的说法，他们在某种主流进步自由派中表现得好得多。

sentences.en: You can imagine the sort of person who watches MSNBC in the suburbs, for instance, who voted for Hillary Clinton or Elizabeth Warren and Joe Biden in 2020.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象那种在郊区看MSNBC的人，例如，他们在2020年投票给了希拉里·克林顿、伊丽莎白·沃伦或乔·拜登。

sentences.en: They're actually quite sympathetic to what the progressives have to say about all of the various issues we just talked about, like Gaza or the Black Lives Matter movement.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上对进步派关于我们刚刚谈到的所有各种议题（如加沙或“黑人的命也是命”运动）的看法非常同情。

sentences.en: They may not be Democratic Socialists, but they are real progressives.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不是民主社会主义者，但他们确实是进步派。

sentences.en: And in the past, they didn't support Bernie Sanders, and they have been voting for mainstream Democrats.
sentences.zh: 在过去，他们不支持伯尼·桑德斯，并且一直投票给主流民主党人。

sentences.en: But now they're pretty disillusioned with the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 但现在他们对民主党相当幻灭。

sentences.en: It's failed to make good on its promise to defeat Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 民主党未能兑现击败唐纳德·特朗普的承诺。

sentences.en: They want to see someone fight back against Donald Trump in Washington.
sentences.zh: 他们希望看到有人在华盛顿对抗唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And they're just looking for a candidate who offers bigger kind of changes to a country that voters have been dissatisfied with for decades.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在寻找一位能为选民几十年来一直感到不满的国家提供更大变革的候选人。

sentences.en: And right now, the Democratic Socialist progressive activist wing of the Democratic Party is offering something like that.
sentences.zh: 而现在，民主党内民主社会主义进步激进派正在提供类似的东西。

sentences.en: And so these voters who have voted maybe for more moderate candidates in the past, they're pretty open to backing progressive candidates today.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些过去可能投给更温和派候选人的选民，如今对支持进步派候选人相当开放。

sentences.zh: 这些人基本上不会被其中一些文化战争的信息所疏远。

sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能喜欢它。

sentences.zh: 他们可能会喜欢。

sentences.zh: 而且他们对民主党建制派如此沮丧，以至于在某些情况下他们想投抗议票。

sentences.en: And I think it could be even more than a protest vote.
sentences.zh: 我认为这甚至可能不仅仅是一张抗议票。

sentences.zh: 他们可能会看着民主社会主义者说，你知道吗？

sentences.zh: 我一直支持全民医疗。

sentences.en: And that's what they say they support, too.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们说他们支持的。

sentences.en: I don't like what Israel is doing.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢以色列在做的事情。

sentences.en: I agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我同意这一点。

sentences.en: So they may not, again, consider themselves Democratic Socialists.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能再次不认为自己是民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: They may not be activists for the Democratic Socialist cause.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不是民主社会主义事业的激进分子。

sentences.en: But they may not see themselves as very different on a long list of issues.
sentences.zh: 但在一长串议题上，他们可能不觉得自己有很大不同。

sentences.en: I guess my question is, is that a winning coalition?
sentences.zh: 我想我的问题是，这是一个能赢的联盟吗？

sentences.en: Is that enough to win in purple places in a general election?
sentences.zh: 这足以在大选中的摇摆地区获胜吗？

sentences.en: In a general election?
sentences.zh: 在大选中？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不能。

sentences.en: I mean, you can win a Democratic primary with a core of Democratic Socialists plus sort of mainstream liberals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以凭借民主社会主义者的核心加上主流自由派赢得民主党初选。

sentences.en: But to win a general election, you need to win a lot more than that.
sentences.zh: 但要赢得大选，你需要赢得比这多得多的支持。

sentences.en: You have to win the rank and file of the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 你必须赢得民主党的中坚力量。

sentences.en: And then a lot of more moderate voters who don't consider themselves Democrats or independents or who may even in some cases be relatively conservative voters.
sentences.zh: 然后还要赢得大量不认为自己是民主党人、是独立选民或者在某些情况下甚至可能是相对保守的温和派选民。

sentences.en: Then does that suggest that these candidates will have to kind of win back those white working class voters, the ones who voted for Trump?
sentences.zh: 那么这是否表明这些候选人将不得不赢回那些白人工人阶级选民，也就是那些投票给特朗普的人？

sentences.en: And if they stick to the economic populism message and deemphasize the other stuff, is that a path forward?
sentences.zh: 如果他们坚持经济民粹主义信息并淡化其他事情，这是一条前进的道路吗？

sentences.en: Do they need to do that to broaden their coalition?
sentences.zh: 他们需要这样做来扩大他们的联盟吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think that's what the progressives see for themselves.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这就是进步派为自己看到的。

sentences.en: I think they want to try and win back some number of white working class or at least working class voters in general with a message focused on economic populism.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们希望通过以经济民粹主义为重点的信息，尝试赢回一定数量的白人工人阶级选民，或者至少是广义上的工人阶级选民。

sentences.en: I don't think that's necessarily very realistic.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不一定是十分现实的。

sentences.en: And you can sort of see that in its own way in these Democratic primaries.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这些民主党初选中以其独特的方式看到这一点。

sentences.en: They can talk about economic populism a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们可以大量谈论经济民粹主义。

sentences.en: They can even make that the focus of their campaigns to the extent they can.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可以把这作为竞选的重点，只要他们能做到这一点。

sentences.en: But they're going to be defined by the broader set of issues that they're associated with and that they're really passionate about.
sentences.zh: 但他们将由他们所关联的、真正热衷的更广泛的议题来定义。

sentences.en: There's not going to be a version of Dr. El-Sayed who doesn't talk about Gaza and who doesn't talk about all the other issues that progressives have been campaigning on for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 不会出现一个不谈论加沙、不谈论进步派过去10年来一直在竞选的所有其他议题的埃尔萨耶德博士版本。

sentences.en: But to win a general election,
sentences.zh: 但要在初选中获胜——抱歉，大选中获胜，

sentences.en: they're probably going to need to win in a fairly conventional way for a Democrat to try and be acceptable enough to voters who are dissatisfied with Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他们可能需要以一种相当传统的方式为民主党赢得胜利，以便让对唐纳德·特朗普不满的选民觉得足够可以接受。

sentences.en: Some of them are working class.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人是工人阶级。

sentences.en: Some of them are rich and affluent.
sentences.zh: 有些人是富裕阶层。

sentences.en: Some of them may be the kind of voters that progressives dream of winning and some of them may bear no resemblance to that.
sentences.zh: 有些人可能是进步派梦想赢得的那种选民，有些人可能与之毫无相似之处。

sentences.en: But they're stuck playing, I think, a fundamentally conventional general election game.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们只能陷入一场根本上传统的大选游戏。

sentences.en: Nate,
sentences.zh: 内特，

sentences.en: another big part of this debate among Democrats is whether these socialists or socialist-adjacent candidates may drag Democrats down in other parts of the country by giving Republicans this opening to cast the entire party as too radical.
sentences.zh: 民主党人这场辩论的另一个重要部分是，这些社会主义者或与社会主义相关联的候选人是否会通过给共和党人提供将整个政党描绘得过于激进的切入点，从而在全国其他地方拖累民主党？

sentences.en: How do you think that dynamic might play out as we get closer to the general?
sentences.zh: 随着我们越来越接近大选，你认为这种动态会如何展开？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's true to some extent.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为在某种程度上确实如此。

sentences.en: When you vote for a Democratic candidate, you're voting both for the person and to put a party in power.
sentences.zh: 当你投票给民主党候选人时，你既是在为这个人投票，也是在为让一个政党掌权投票。

sentences.en: And to the extent voters sour on putting the Democratic Party in power because they perceive it as being farther to the left than they are,
sentences.zh: 如果选民因为认为民主党比他们想象的更向左倾而对让民主党掌权感到失望，

sentences.en: that could hurt Democratic candidates in parts of the country who have nothing to do with the progressive left.
sentences.zh: 这可能会伤害全国各地与进步左翼毫无关系的民主党候选人。

sentences.en: That said, I think in most of these races that Democratic candidates will succeed in defining themselves,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为在大多数这些竞选中，民主党候选人将成功地定义自己，

sentences.en: certainly the strong Democratic candidates with their own individual brands who have the resources to air television advertisements about themselves,
sentences.zh: 当然，那些拥有自己独立品牌、有资源播放关于自己的电视广告的强有力民主党候选人，

sentences.en: they have an opportunity to define themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们有机会定义自己。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't expect it to prevent more moderate Democrats from winning in much of the country, even if it is undoubtedly some additional burden that they have to overcome.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会指望这会阻止更温和的民主党人在全国大部分地区获胜，即使这无疑是他们必须克服的某种额外负担。

sentences.en: Obviously, we spent this time looking at, as you said, idiosyncratic races.
sentences.zh: 很明显，我们花时间研究了正如你所说的那样独特的竞选。

sentences.en: So I don't want to extrapolate too much here.
sentences.zh: 所以我不想在这里做过多的外推。

sentences.en: But given the broader dynamics that you've laid out about this left-wing coalition,
sentences.zh: 但鉴于你所阐述的关于这个左翼联盟的更广泛动态，

sentences.en: I wonder how you're also thinking about its place in the future of the party beyond these midterMs.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你如何看待它在这次中期选举之后在党内未来的地位？

sentences.en: Like, crystal ball, a little bit for me.
sentences.zh: 比如，为我预测一下未来。

sentences.en: There's an unmistakable trend towards the progressive left and Democratic politics.
sentences.zh: 朝向进步左翼和民主党政治的趋势是不可否认的。

sentences.en: We've talked about that already.
sentences.zh: 我们之前已经讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: And as generations turn over and more young people enter the Democratic electorate and as more older moderates age out of the Democratic electorate,
sentences.zh: 随着世代交替，更多年轻人进入民主党选民阵营，以及更多年长温和派退出民主党选民阵营，

sentences.en: I think it's possible we could see this trend continue.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有可能看到这种趋势继续下去。

sentences.en: It would not surprise me to see a candidate the progressive left win the Democratic nomination in 2028 if they have a strong enough candidate to pull it off or if the establishment is disorganized like it was in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 如果进步左翼有一个足够强大的候选人来完成这一目标，或者如果建制派像在威斯康星州那样一盘散沙，我不会对2028年进步左翼候选人赢得民主党提名感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Now, that said, it doesn't make it inevitable that progressive activists will take over the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这并不意味着进步派激进分子接管民主党是不可避免的。

sentences.en: Mainstream Democrats will try and co-opt elements of this message.
sentences.zh: 主流民主党人将尝试吸收这一信息的元素。

sentences.en: They're going to try and appeal on the same kind of themes about economic populism.
sentences.zh: 他们将尝试围绕经济民粹主义的相同主题进行诉求。

sentences.en: We just saw Gavin Newsom say the divide in American politics today isn't between left and right.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚看到加文·纽森说，今天美国政治的分歧不在于左右之间。

sentences.en: It's between top and down.
sentences.zh: 而在于高层和底层之间。

sentences.en: Mainstream Democrats are getting a message here.
sentences.zh: 主流民主党人在这里接收到了一个信息。

sentences.en: And this is pretty common in American politics, that activists elevate an issue and the mainstream of the party ultimately subsumes it.
sentences.zh: 这在美国政治中很常见，激进分子提出一个议题，而政党主流最终将其包容吸收。

sentences.en: But then what would happen to all of the more hardcore supporters of that socialist DSA platform?
sentences.zh: 但随后，所有那些社会主义DSA纲领的更死忠支持者会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: I can't imagine that they would get on board for a much more diluted version of the thing that has them so energized.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象他们会接受那个让他们如此热血沸腾的事物的严重稀释版本。

sentences.en: This is a cop-out answer, but it will obviously vary from person to person, group to group.
sentences.zh: 这是一个敷衍的回答，但它显然会因人而异、因群体而异。

sentences.en: There are going to be some diehard Democratic socialists who will say that any person who doesn't reject the system of capitalism is complicit in the oppression of the working classes around the world,
sentences.zh: 会有一些死硬的民主社会主义者说，任何不拒绝资本主义制度的人都是世界各地工人阶级受压迫的同谋，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: There are also going to be progressives who understand that it's important to work within the Democratic Party to gradually change it.
sentences.zh: 也有一部分进步派人士明白，在民主党内部通过工作来逐渐改变它是很重要的。

sentences.en: Over time, in different cases, the relative balance of which two paths different parts of the left take is going to vary.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，在不同的情况下，左翼不同部分采取的这两条路径的相对平衡也会有所不同。

sentences.en: If Gavin Newsom wins the Democratic nomination because he adopted a buzzword about top versus bottom, it's going to be a little different than if it's, say,
sentences.zh: 如果加文·纽森因为采用了关于底层对抗顶层的时髦词汇而赢得民主党提名，这将会与，比方说……

sentences.en: a John Ossoff who centers corruption and taking on the billionaires in this campaign, right?
sentences.zh: 像乔·奥索夫这样在竞选时把反腐败和对抗亿万富翁作为核心的候选人有些不同，对吧？

sentences.en: So there are a lot of subtleties here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有很多微妙之处。

sentences.en: But I think over the long run, the thing that's sort of guaranteed is that if the progressive left becomes strong enough in the Democratic Party,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得从长远来看，某种程度上可以保证的是，如果进步派左翼在民主党内变得足够强大，

sentences.en: it is going to change the Democratic Party one way or another.
sentences.zh: 它势必会以这样或那样的方式改变民主党。

sentences.en: If the mainstream of the party resists it, that's when you have the opportunity for a real hostile takeover like what happened to the Republicans.
sentences.zh: 如果党内主流势力进行抵抗，那就会迎来像共和党那样真正被敌意收购的机会。

sentences.en: I think it's too early to say whether we're going to see something more like a hostile takeover or more like the mainstream of the Democratic Party letting the Democratic socialists in and gradually allow it to change the party.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在说我们是会看到更类似于敌意收购的情况，还是更类似于民主党主流接纳民主社会主义者并逐渐允许其改变政党，还为时过早。

sentences.en: In some cases, you'll see some of both.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，你会看到两者兼有。

sentences.en: I think over the medium term, I would expect to see the mainstream of the Democratic Party try and embrace economic populism, try and take a more anti-Israel stance.
sentences.zh: 我认为在中期来看，我预计民主党主流会试图拥抱经济民粹主义，并尝试采取更加反以色列的立场。

sentences.en: And that may be enough to prevent a true takeover of the Democratic Party by Democratic socialists, even as the Democratic Party moves to the left as a consequence.
sentences.zh: 即使民主党因此向左转，这或许也足以阻止民主社会主义者真正接管民主党。

sentences.en: But the natural tendency for a party is to try and assimilate all of its parts and to forge a coalition, to use a word that we've used probably too many times in this episode.
sentences.zh: 但政党的天性总是试图同化其所有部分并建立联盟——用一个我们在这集里可能用得有点太多的词。

sentences.en: And that's the natural way for the party to end up.
sentences.zh: 而这正是政党最终的自然归宿。

sentences.en: Well, Nate, I love having you in my coalition as a colleague.
sentences.zh: 好了，内特，很高兴我的联盟里有你这样的同事。

sentences.en: And thanks for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到节目中。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 喂。

sentences.en: Hi, this is Jodi.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是乔迪。

sentences.en: Hi, Jodi.
sentences.zh: 嗨，乔迪。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: This is Caitlin calling for The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是代表《纽约时报》打来的凯特琳。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm doing well.
sentences.zh: 我挺好的。

sentences.en: I really appreciate you taking some time to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你花时间跟我聊聊。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're in an interesting state, no?
sentences.zh: 对啊，我们处在一个很有意思的州，不是吗？

sentences.en: You really are.
sentences.zh: 你们确实是。

sentences.en: How does it feel?
sentences.zh: 感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: It's stressful, totally stressful, because there's so much at stake.
sentences.zh: 压力山大，完全是压力山大，因为有太多利益攸关了。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, one day after the Democratic primary for governor in Wisconsin, Daily Producer Caitlin O'Keefe called voters there to understand how they were processing the results.
sentences.zh: 周三，也就是威斯康星州长民主党初选的第二天，节目制作人凯特琳·奥基夫致电那里的选民，以了解他们如何看待初选结果。

sentences.en: Can you tell me who you voted for in the primary on Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我你在周二的初选中投给了谁吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I voted for Francesca Holland.
sentences.zh: 是的，我投给了弗朗西斯卡·霍兰。

sentences.en: Francesca was my choice.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯卡是我的选择。

sentences.en: Ultimately, I ended up voting for David Crowley.
sentences.zh: 最终，我还是投票给了大卫·克劳利。

sentences.en: I voted for David Crowley.
sentences.zh: 我投给了大卫·克劳利。

sentences.en: I just thought more important than voting for exactly who I'd be more passionate about.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，比起投票给你个人更有热情的对象，这更为重要。

sentences.en: We need to get somebody in there that can win the race.
sentences.zh: 我们需要选出一个能够赢得这场竞选的人。

sentences.en: When I saw that Crowley had won with just over 3,000 votes shy, it was a huge sense of relief for me.
sentences.zh: 当我看到克劳利以仅落后三千多票的微弱优势获胜时，我感到如释重负。

sentences.en: But a little bit of anxiety that we got that close.
sentences.zh: 但也有一点点险险过关的焦虑。

sentences.en: I really appreciated the progressive views on affordable health care, universal child care, public schools, the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 我真的很赞赏关于负担得起的医疗保健、全民托儿服务、公立学校以及最低工资的进步政策。

sentences.en: My two daughters are middle income and are struggling.
sentences.zh: 我的两个女儿属于中等收入人群，生活得很艰难。

sentences.en: And I don't see a way out of it.
sentences.zh: 而且我看不出有什么出路。

sentences.en: My grandkids, they're having such a hard time finding jobs.
sentences.zh: 我的孙辈们，他们找工作太艰难了。

sentences.en: It didn't used to be that way.
sentences.zh: 过去可不是这样的。

sentences.en: So I'm just not for the establishment right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在就是不支持建制派。

sentences.en: I feel like they just keep going along the same path.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们只是在沿着同一条老路走下去。

sentences.en: I think we need to wipe this late clean.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们需要一笔勾销。

sentences.en: Start over.
sentences.zh: 重新开始。

sentences.en: What would you say to somebody who looks at Hong's loss in Wisconsin and thinks this is proof that the Democratic Socialists of America and that platform can't win across the country?
sentences.zh: 对于那些看到洪在威斯康星州落败，并认为这证明了美国民主社会主义者及其纲领无法在全国范围内获胜的人，你会说些什么？

sentences.en: Good ideas have been coming from the progressive movement for years.
sentences.zh: 进步运动多年来一直在提出好的理念。

sentences.en: And sometimes they get more footing.
sentences.zh: 有时它们能获得更多支持。

sentences.en: Sometimes they don't.
sentences.zh: 有时则不然。

sentences.en: They've got to wait their time.
sentences.zh: 它们必须等待时机。

sentences.en: I think there are repairs we can make to our capitalist system without completely upending everything.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以在不彻底颠覆一切的情况下对资本主义制度进行修补。

sentences.en: When essentially your platform is just tear it all down and rebuild.
sentences.zh: 当你的纲领本质上只是摧毁一切然后重建时，

sentences.en: I don't think we need to tear it all down and rebuild.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们需要摧毁一切然后重建。

sentences.en: I think that we need to prepare our democracy in progress and this experiment that we're on.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要修复我们的民主、进步以及我们正在进行的这场实验。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: The Trump administration plans to spend millions of dollars equipping immigration officers with gloves that can deliver electric shocks on contact to induce compliance.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府计划花费数百万美元为移民官员配备接触时可通过电击促使对方配合的手套。

sentences.en: The gloves, which are sometimes referred to as stun gloves, take only a second to be switched on by pressing a button.
sentences.zh: 这种手套有时被称为电击手套，只需按一下按钮，一秒钟即可开启。

sentences.en: And they're made by a Kentucky company called Compliant Technologies.
sentences.zh: 它们由肯塔基州一家名为“合规技术”的公司制造。

sentences.en: The company says that the gloves emit a much lower voltage than a taser.
sentences.zh: 该公司表示，这种手套释放的电压远低于泰瑟枪。

sentences.en: The Homeland Security Department described the gloves as a de-escalation device,
sentences.zh: 国土安全部将这些手套描述为一种缓和冲突的设备，

sentences.en: but didn't answer questions about whether they might be used to apprehend people or in encounters with protesters.
sentences.zh: 但没有回答关于它们是否会被用于抓捕人员或在与抗议者冲突时使用的问题。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Caitlin O'Keefe, Jack DeSidoro, and Carlos Prieto.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由凯特琳·奥基夫、杰克·德西多罗和卡洛斯·普里托制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Rob Zipko and Paige Cowett, with help from Lizzo Baylin.

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是遮光睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会一黑就晕过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线条件？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们习惯喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
